Startup splash diagnostic log

Startup logging is enabled in this build and records startup on the device automatically, without a separate capture step. After installing over the app, finish any welcome flow and dismiss the splash animation, then close the app and open it from the home screen icon. After the flash appears, return promptly, export the most recent hour of logs and share it with the developer. Logs are never uploaded automatically. A screen recording is needed to verify the system launch screen.

Regex replacement guide
Tutorial
AI prompt
Step 1: Capture the text you want to replace

Take a screenshot of the reading page that shows the text to remove or replace and a few surrounding lines. If similar text appears in several forms, take multiple screenshots.\n\nSend the screenshots to the AI you use and describe your goal, for example: Remove the ad notice but keep the surrounding text, or replace both 小明 and 小铭 with 阿明. Make sure the text is legible. You can paste the original text instead if screenshots are inconvenient.
Step 2: Copy the prompt and send it with screenshots

Use the button below to copy the complete prompt. Send it with the screenshots and desired changes to an AI that can read images. The prompt describes the supported Lumi regex syntax, replacement format and limitations. The AI can construct rules based on the screenshot. Visual line wraps are not necessarily real newlines; ask the AI to confirm unclear text first.
Copy the complete prompt
Copied. Ready to send to AI
Prompt for AI
Paste the result back into Lumi

Return to Replacement cleanup → Add rule → Regex. Copy the AI-generated search expression into Find and the replacement text into Replace with. Do not include code fences or explanations. Leave Replace with empty to delete matched text.\n\nCurrently, rules are pasted into these two fields; no file import is needed. Check the current chapter preview, then tap the check mark to save and enable the rule and this book. If the result is wrong, give the AI the source text, error and expected result so it can revise the rule.
First: Find a pattern of text and handle it consistently

Plain replacement is for fixed text, such as changing 小明 to 阿明. Regex replacement uses a matching pattern to find similar text, such as both 小明 and 小铭, or an entire line beginning with 本章未完.

Plain and regex rules are stored in a shared rule library for all books, so they do not need to be reentered. New books and rules are disabled by default. Each book can enable individual rules and choose their order. Editing or deleting a rule affects all books using it.

Cleanup changes only the visible reading text of books where it is enabled; the original file is not modified. Turn off the per-book switch or an individual rule to restore the original text.
First-time setup: 5 steps

1. Return to Replacement cleanup and tap Add rule.
2. Choose Regex. Enter only the search expression from the examples below into Find. Do not include quotes, code fences or /…/g.
3. Fill in Replace with. Leave it truly empty to remove matching text. Do not enter the words Leave empty. The rule name is optional.
4. Check the current chapter preview. Review the match count and before/after text. The preview shows the area around the first match only; it does not mean there is only one match in the entire book.
5. Tap the check mark at the upper right to save, then enable both the rule and the In this book switch.

Open this tutorial from the i icon at the upper right of the create/edit screen and resume editing afterward.
Common regex symbols

. Any character except newline by default
[明铭] Either 明 or 铭
[0-9] or \d One ASCII digit; use [０-９] for full-width digits
[一二三四五六七八九十百千万]+ One or more listed Chinese numeral characters
\s Whitespace, including spaces, tabs and newlines
[ \t] ASCII space or tab only; does not cross lines
\S Any non-whitespace character
* Repeat the preceding item zero or more times
+ Repeat one or more times
? Optional: zero or one occurrence
{2,4} Repeat 2 to 4 times; {2} means exactly twice
A|B Match either A or B
(…) Capture a group for use in replacement
^ / $ Start/end of a text fragment, or of a line with (?m)

For example, [0-9]+ matches 1, 25 and 108. Square brackets select one character, while parentheses group a sequence.
How to match the symbols themselves

In Find, the characters . * + ? ( ) [ ] { } ^ $ | and the backslash have special meanings. To match them literally, usually prefix them with a backslash.

Examples: \. finds a dot, \( finds an opening parenthesis, \[ finds an opening square bracket, and \\ finds one backslash. Enter \d directly in the field, not \\d as in programming source code.

To remove a fixed phrase including punctuation, Plain mode is usually easier and requires no escaping. Chinese parentheses （ ） and book-title brackets 《 》 can be entered directly.
Ready-to-use examples
Choose Regex mode for all examples. Long-press an expression to select and copy it, then adapt it to the book. Where an example says Leave empty, do not enter any characters.
1. Normalize different spellings of a character name
[明铭] matches one of those two characters, so it finds both 小明 and 小铭, but not 小红.
2. Remove an entire line beginning with a notice

(?m) makes ^ match the beginning of every line. [ \\t]* permits leading spaces, | selects one of the notice phrases, and the rest matches to the end of that line.\n\nUse this only if the entire line is a notice or advertisement. If normal text follows the notice, it will also be removed. The newline itself is preserved, possibly leaving an empty line.
3. Remove advertising tags in square brackets

\\[ and \\] match the literal square brackets. [^\\]\\r\\n]* matches any character except a closing bracket or newline. This removes only the bracketed phrase beginning with 广告：, while trying to leave the surrounding text intact.
4. Collapse repeated ASCII spaces
{2,} means two or more spaces. Enter one actual ASCII space in Replace with. Full-width spaces and newlines are not affected.
5. Preserve chapter numbers while changing notation

([0-9]+) captures the chapter number as group 1. $1 in Replace with inserts that number. \\s* permits whitespace between 第, the number and 章. This example handles ASCII digits, not Chinese numerals such as 第十二章. It only changes visible body text and does not rebuild the table of contents.
6. Ignore English letter case
(?i) makes subsequent matching case-insensitive, so VIP, Vip and vip all match. This example also replaces those letters inside longer words. To match only separate words, use (?i)\\bvip\\b.
Leave empty (enter nothing)
One ASCII space
Capture groups and Replace with syntax

Parentheses in Find number capture groups in order of their opening brackets: $1 is group 1, $2 is group 2, and $0 is the entire match. For example, Find (小)(明) and Replace with $2$1 changes 小明 into 明小. (?:…) groups text without assigning a capture number. Only reference groups that actually exist.

Replace with is not another regex: $1 inserts a captured group, \$ outputs a dollar sign, and \\ outputs one backslash. To output the literal characters $1, enter \$1.

Do not enter \n in Replace with expecting a newline. The backslash escapes the next character here, so \n outputs the letter n. Enter an actual newline when needed.
Line matching, multiline matching and scope

(?m): Makes ^ and $ match the beginning and end of each line. It does not let the dot match newlines.
(?s): Lets the dot . match newlines too. Cross-line deletion can remove too much; prefer patterns that stay on one line.
.*: Greedy, matching as much as possible. For example, 【.*】 on 【甲】【乙】 matches the whole span.
.*?: Non-greedy, matching as little as possible. 【.*?】 matches 【甲】 and 【乙】 separately.

Automatic visual line wrapping is not necessarily a newline. EPUB and MOBI replacement runs on supported text fragments and cannot cross independent paragraphs, images or other boundaries. Even (?s) cannot guarantee matching across these boundaries. Do not treat cleanup rules as an HTML tag editor.
How do multiple rules interact?

Rule content is shared across books, but each book has its own enabled rules and order. Rules run from top to bottom, and each later rule sees the text produced by previous rules. For example, after changing 小明 to 阿明, a later rule looking for 小明 will not match. Move rules up or down to adjust their order.\n\nGive each rule one purpose and a clear name, then inspect previews one by one. If the result is wrong, disable a suspicious rule or turn off the book-level switch to restore original text.
When nothing matches or an error appears

• No matches in this chapter: Verify that the target text is present. Check whitespace, newlines, full-width versus ASCII characters and case. Start with a short pattern, then add conditions. Saved rules also apply to other chapters.
• Invalid regex: Check matching parentheses and escaping. The engine uses RE2/J and does not support lookarounds such as (?=…), (?!…), (?<=…), (?<!…) or backreferences like \1 in Find. Captured groups can still be used as $1 in Replace with.
• Invalid capture group: For example, using $2 when only group 1 exists, entering $ alone, or ending with a backslash. Use \$ to output a dollar sign.
• No visible change after saving: Check the book and rule switches, their order, and that you tapped the save check mark. A zero-width match such as ^ alone does not insert text.
• Too much removed: Avoid starting with .* or (?s). Define precise match boundaries and inspect the preview. A preview around the first match cannot prove that all matches are correct.
